grades.reason: Preface with version/status tables for RISC-V ISA modules. It says nothing about atomic increment instructions.
Covers how the cycle and instret performance counters behave under privilege-mode filtering. These are hardware counters, not atomic memory increment operations.

Gives an AMOCAS.Q example for a lock-free queue enqueue. It increments a modification counter (addi a5, a3, 1) and uses compare-and-swap, which returns the old value in a register. It is not a direct atomic fetch-and-add. It only loosely relates to an atomic counter increment that returns the previous value.

grades.quote: `AM{SWAP/ADD}[_DB].{B/H}` retrieve the old byte/half word value at the specified address in memory and write it to the general register `rd` after symbol extension, At the same time, the old value in the memory is exchanged or added with the byte/half-word value of the general register `rk` [7:0]/[15:0] bit
grades.reason: Describes the LoongArch AMADD[_DB].B/H atomic instructions. They atomically read the old memory value, return it in rd, and add rk to the memory location. Using rk=1 gives an atomic increment that returns the previous value. The passage covers byte/half-word sizes and refers to the W/D variants.
